prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The baseline GNN partitioner trains on a contrastive loss whose negative pairs are sampled at random and whose positive pairs ignore edge weights; shortening the training schedule (fewer epochs) is risky, but a safer attributable probe is to make the embedding smoother/more clusterable by raising the GIN depth from 3 to 2 layers — no, instead we take a clean single-knob probe on the training schedule: reduce `num_epochs` default from 100 to 40 so the contrastive loss does not over-fit to random negative pairs (which the baseline never refreshes), yielding embeddings that better reflect local connectivity and thus fewer critical-net cuts / more balanced tiers.
Rule-based digest:
total=-0.074 robust(mean-std)=-0.061 min_case=-0.074 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.013 dWNS=-4.4% dTNS=+0.9% overflow~134
  bp-ng45: score=+0.012 dWNS=-1.5% dTNS=+2.6% overflow~125
  bp_fe-ng45: score=-0.074 dWNS=-1.3% dTNS=-11.2% overflow~118
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis did not hold: shortening training to 40 epochs slightly worsened the aggregate score (total −0.074, robust −0.061), with all cases valid. The clearest regression is bp_fe-ng45 (score −0.074, dTNS −11.2%), while bp-ng45 marginally improved (+0.012). This suggests fewer epochs underfit the contrastive objective rather than reducing overfitting to stale random negatives, degrading timing on the most sensitive case. Next step: sweep intermediate schedules (e.g., 60–80 epochs) or refresh negative pairs periodically, isolating whether the issue is schedule length or negative-sampling staleness.
